clue.text: Enable me to return old whiskey in person? Just half!

indicators.note: returning sends the word me back the other way, so it is read from right to left
in puts the old-and-whiskey pair inside the shortened word that follows
just half of a six-letter word keeps only its first three letters

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A drinker pictures turning up with an old whiskey in person, but only managing half of the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' and 'Just half' are the signals; 'in' puts the old-whiskey pair inside the halved word. 'whiskey' is W from the NATO phonetic alphabet, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To empower someone is to give them the authority or means to act, which is what enabling them does.

clue.text: Editor with religious book missing cover? It's ok to scoff

indicators.note: a cover sits on top, so the top letter of the book's name is dropped

parts.note: the Bible is the holy book of Christianity

explanation.surface: An editor reads the Bible without its jacket and wonders whether mocking it is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoff' looks like mocking but is slang for eating greedily; 'missing cover' strips the B from BIBLE to give IBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is fit to be eaten, safe to gobble down, is edible; scoff is British slang for eating.

clue.text: Dad left rook under a tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the rook's letter comes below the a

parts.note: pop is an informal word for a father
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A father abandons a chess rook beneath a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The poplar is a tall, fast-growing deciduous tree, so it is an example of the general word.

clue.text: Savage birds on southern wasteland

parts.note: savage and wild both mean untamed or fierce
ernes are sea eagles, crossword favourites

explanation.surface: Fierce birds descend on a barren stretch of land in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilderness is an uncultivated, uninhabited region, essentially a wasteland.

clue.text: Australian animal on street picked up germs

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it, so the street's letters are read upwards, reversed

explanation.surface: A kangaroo on the road catches some infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'germs' looks like microbes but means origins, as in the germ of an idea; 'picked up' turns ST into TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Germs in the sense of beginnings or seeds of something are its roots, the sources from which it grows.

clue.text: Wanted something done about gentleman

indicators.note: about means going around, so the deed's letters surround the gentleman's title

parts.note: a deed is an act, something that has been done
sir is the polite title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A man was sought for some act involving a gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Desired and wanted are synonyms, both describing something longed for.

clue.text: Pants could fit if nothing's gone knotty

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or poor, so the letters are badly arranged
gone says the nothing has left the word could

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Trousers that could fit if only there were nothing in the way have become tangled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers but is the anagram signal; 'gone' takes the O from COULD, leaving CULD to mix with FIT and IF.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem is a hard, complicated one, so knotty means hard to solve.

clue.text: Lay off wine

definitions.meaning: to dismiss a worker from a job
an old word for a dry white wine from Spain or the Canaries, as in Falstaff's favourite

explanation.surface: Give up drinking wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing staff is giving them the sack, and the old Spanish fortified wine was also called by this name.

clue.text: Response from Royal Engineers before battle

indicators.note: in a down clue the engineers come first, ahead of the battle

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
action means fighting, as in killed in action

explanation.surface: Army engineers respond before going into battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is a reply or answer to something that has happened, so it is a synonym of the definition.

clue.text: Good-looking person shedding last hair — misery!

indicators.note: shedding last drops the final letter of the word for the attractive person

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A beautiful person losing their hair is in despair.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is great suffering or anguish, which matches misery as a synonym.

clue.text: Drive Hillman, perhaps, with the Parisian in reverse

parts.note: the Hillman Imp was a small British car of the 1960s

indicators.note: in reverse says the French article is read backwards

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Driving a Hillman car around Paris while backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' sits beside a car and looks like motoring, but it means to push someone on; 'in reverse' turns the French article round.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to urge or force someone forward, just as to drive them does.

clue.text: Rotten and in charge, this person also removes ordinary administrators

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten
the setter refers to themselves as I

indicators.note: removes says a letter is taken away from the word also

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in the old O level

explanation.surface: Corrupt and in charge, someone sacks ordinary managers too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removes' takes O out of ALSO, leaving ALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Officials are people holding posts of authority, who run and administer organisations.

clue.text: What government needs desperately is help, dear

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild, frantic action, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A plea to the authorities, dear, for help that is badly needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Governing requires someone to guide and direct, the quality of leading people.

clue.text: Leading performer's heavenly body

definitions.meaning: the headline act in a show or film
a luminous sun in the night sky

explanation.surface: The lead actor has a celestial physique.
explanation.definitionFit: The top-billed actor is called this, and so are the glowing suns seen in the night sky.

clue.text: Rubbish — spare me hot air

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb means to trash, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests at nonsense, asking to be spared hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot air' looks like the definition, but only 'air' is; 'hot' is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere is the mass of air surrounding the earth, and also a mood or feeling in a place.

clue.text: Rows after this month's orders

indicators.note: after puts the rows at the end, following this month's letters

parts.note: inst, short for instant, is old business-letter style for this month
ructions are noisy quarrels

explanation.surface: Arguments follow this month's commands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inst' (instant) dated a letter to the current month, as in 'your letter of the 5th inst'.
explanation.definitionFit: Instructions are directions telling someone what to do, which is what orders are.

clue.text: Buy and sell endlessly — one into bad habit

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the word for buying and selling

parts.note: to trade is to buy and sell goods
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone told to stop dealing slips back into a bad habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TRADE to TRAD; 'bad' rearranges I and INTO to make ITION.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a custom or practice handed down and repeated, a habitual way of doing things.

clue.text: China follows Eastern Standard Time, I guess

indicators.note: follows puts the friend's word after the time zone and the I

parts.note: EST is the abbreviation for Eastern Standard Time
china is rhyming slang for mate: china plate, mate

explanation.surface: China keeps to the American eastern time zone, the speaker supposes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but is Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with 'mate', a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to make a rough calculation or judgement, which is to guess.

clue.text: Jumpers maybe the least unravelled

indicators.note: unravelled is undone, like knitting, so the letters are taken apart and remade

explanation.surface: Sweaters, perhaps, that have come the least undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumpers' and 'unravelled' suggest knitted sweaters; here jumpers are sportspeople, and 'maybe' marks them as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: High jumpers and long jumpers are examples of track and field sportspeople.

clue.text: Joy was placed next to single small group

indicators.note: next to says the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: sat means was seated or set down
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a faction is a group within a larger body

explanation.surface: Delight at being seated beside one small party.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfaction is the pleasure felt when a wish is fulfilled, akin to joy.

clue.text: Confusion no good in story

indicators.note: in places the two abbreviations inside the word for story

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A muddle with nothing good in the narrative.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle is a confused, jumbled state or muddle, so it means confusion.

clue.text: Snake about to be enthralled by alien's appearance

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive by, so the about letter is held within the alien

parts.note: ET is the alien from the Spielberg film
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A snake captivated by an alien's looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralled by' puts C inside ET to make ECT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is the look or outward appearance of something, as in a building's aspect.

clue.text: Python lay on one's oars

definitions.meaning: Eric, a member of the Monty Python comedy team
an idiom meaning to stop working and rest

explanation.surface: A snake lies on the rower's oars.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric of Monty Python shares the surname, and resting on oars means doing nothing, being inactive.

clue.text: Drunk, pa's despair vanishes

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and unsteady, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Father's misery when intoxicated simply fades away.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to go out of sight, which is exactly what something that disappears does.

clue.text: Insist resistance cuts fever

indicators.note: cuts means slices into, so the resistance letter goes inside the fever

parts.note: ague is an old word for a malarial fever
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A demand that resistance lowers a temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue a point is to maintain or assert it firmly, so to insist on it.

clue.text: Climbing mountain for a bet

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads upwards, so the mountain's name is reversed

parts.note: Etna is the volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: Climbing a mountain on a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a stake put into the pot before cards are dealt in poker, a wager.

clue.text: Taking part in a tango with tense conclusion

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Joining in a tango that ends tensely.
explanation.definitionFit: Being present at an event, as in attending a class, means taking part in it.

clue.text: Not totally keen to catch large bird

indicators.note: to catch means to hold inside, so the large letter is enclosed
not totally drops the last letter of the word for keen

parts.note: eager means keen

explanation.surface: A not-quite-enthusiastic predator tries to catch a big bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey, an example of the general word.

clue.text: Oriental festival name?

parts.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival

explanation.surface: What a spring holiday might be called.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern both describe things from the East, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Base allowed to retain soldiers for a bit

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

indicators.note: to retain means to keep within, so the soldiers sit inside

parts.note: let means allowed
men is a common word for soldiers

explanation.surface: A military base lets troops stay for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a military camp, but it is the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is a component or small part of something, as in an element of truth, so a bit.
